title: SpaceX Is About to Become the Biggest IPO in History — and Indian Investors Are Already Circling
excerpt: Elon Musk's rocket company is targeting a $1.75 trillion Nasdaq debut on June 12. For India's retail investors and its own space ambitions, the ripple effects will be enormous.
body:
When SpaceX's S-1 prospectus landed on May 19, it was not just a financial filing — it was a declaration of intent. The company founded by Elon Musk to colonise Mars is now asking Wall Street to value it at $1.75 trillion, which would make its June 12 Nasdaq debut the largest initial public offering in history, eclipsing Saudi Aramco's $29.4 billion raise in 2019 by a factor of nearly three.

The numbers are staggering. SpaceX reported $18.5 billion in revenue for 2025, driven overwhelmingly by Starlink, its satellite internet constellation that now serves more than 10 million subscribers across 100 countries. The company holds 18,712 Bitcoin on its balance sheet, valued at roughly $1.29 billion. Goldman Sachs leads a syndicate of 21 underwriters, and the offering — internally codenamed "Project Apex" — aims to raise up to $80 billion, with 30 percent of shares reportedly earmarked for retail investors.

For Musk, the IPO is also a consolidation play. In February, SpaceX absorbed xAI, his artificial intelligence venture, in a deal valued at $1.25 trillion. The merged entity now spans rocket launches, satellite broadband, AI data centres, and what Musk calls "orbital compute infrastructure." The dual-class share structure gives him 85.1 percent voting control through Class B shares, ensuring that public shareholders will have minimal say over strategy — a point Musk has made with characteristic bluntness, warning investors not to expect "pandering."

## What It Means for India's Markets

The ripple effects for Indian investors are already visible. On the National Stock Exchange, shares of Indian space companies Skyroot Aerospace and HAL surged in anticipation of a "space sector re-rating." Indian retail investors with US brokerage accounts — a category that has grown tenfold since 2020, now exceeding 2.5 million active accounts on platforms like Vested, INDmoney, and Groww — are the most enthusiastic international cohort positioning for the listing.

But the bigger story for India may be Starlink. Despite years of regulatory delay, SpaceX's satellite internet service remains in a holding pattern over the subcontinent, caught between TRAI's spectrum allocation debates and the lobbying power of Mukesh Ambani's Jio, which has pushed for spectrum auctions rather than administrative allocation. The IPO filing reveals that India is listed among Starlink's "priority expansion markets" for 2026-27. If the regulatory logjam breaks, Starlink could bring high-speed internet to the 300 million Indians still without reliable broadband — a prospect that excites rural development advocates and terrifies incumbent telecoms in equal measure.

## The Diaspora Factor

Indian-origin engineers comprise a significant share of SpaceX's 13,000-strong workforce, particularly in propulsion systems, software engineering, and Starlink's ground infrastructure division. Several senior leaders, including VP of Satellite Engineering Rajeev Badyal (who returned to SpaceX in 2023 after a brief departure), have been instrumental in Starlink's technical architecture. For the Indian diaspora in America's tech corridors, the IPO represents not just a financial opportunity but a validation of their contributions to what may become the world's most valuable company.

## The Sceptics' Case

Not everyone on Wall Street is convinced. At nearly 100 times revenue, SpaceX's valuation assumes sustained exponential growth in both Starlink subscriptions and government launch contracts — assumptions that could falter if competitors like Amazon's Project Kuiper gain ground or if Starship's development timeline slips further. The company's decision to bundle xAI's losses into the same entity adds opacity to the financials.

But for now, the momentum is unmistakable. As AT&T, T-Mobile, and Verizon scramble to form an unprecedented joint venture to counter Starlink's expansion — announced just days before the IPO filing — even SpaceX's rivals are acknowledging what the market already seems to believe: that the gatekeeper to space is about to become the gatekeeper to the future of connectivity itself.
